honesty: Bun:sqlite is sync; JS is single-threaded. The Promise.all-batched dispatcher does not unlock real CPU parallelism today — every handler resolves synchronously when its map callback fires. The win comes from skipping per-feature SELECT lookups and from caching engaged-handler helpers, not from the batching itself.

Promise.all batching is structural prep for a future async-handler upgrade (e.g. a routing handler that fetches an external embedding). When that lands, the batch gate becomes real parallelism with no further dispatcher rewrite.

The 5–12% speedup is real but modest. Most of the per-feature cost lives inside the engine handlers (routing alone is ~117ms of the ~250ms hot path), and those handlers can't be reordered without breaking receipt determinism. To unlock substantially more we'd need either: (a) routing-engine workset caching for the identical-query case, or (b) worker threads with per-worker SQLite connections (architectural change).
